questions.question: The Union Budget, 2020-21, increased deposit insurance coverage for bank deposits to Rs. _______ per depositor.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 lakh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Union Budget 2020-21 announced that the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) has been permitted to increase deposit insurance coverage **to Rs. 5 lakh per depositor from Rs. 1 lakh previously. **
 
• If a customer’s deposit amount crosses Rs 5 lakh in a single bank, only up to Rs 5 lakh, including the principal and interest, will be paid by the DICGC if the bank turns bankrupt.
 
• It was established in 1978 after the merger of Deposit Insurance Corporation (DIC) and Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Ltd. (CGCI) after the passing of the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act, 1961 by the Parliament.
 
• It is a wholly-owned arm of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), which offers deposit insurance. 
 
• It ensures deposit accounts, such as savings, current, recurring, and fixed deposits up to a limit of Rs 5 lakh per account holder of a bank. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Union Budget was structured on the overall theme of “Ease of Living".
 
• The nominal growth rate of GDP is expected to be 10% in 2020-21.
 
• A total of Rs. 64,180 crores to be spent on healthcare.
 
• Defence gets Rs 3.37 lakh crore as the defence budget.
 
• The allocation for higher education is Rs. 39466.52 crores, up from Rs. 38317.01 crore the previous year. 
 
• As compared to the previous year, there has been a rise of around Rs.1149.51 crore.

questions.question: What is the traditional bamboo dance of Mizoram called?
questions.solution:

• It consists of usually six to eight people holding a pair of bamboo staves onto another stick of bamboo positioned horizontally on the ground.

questions.question: Which of the following is the smallest Union Territory of India in terms of area?

options.text: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshadweep.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Lakshadweep is the smallest union territory of India and its total surface area is just 32 km2.
 
• Lakshadweep is an archipelago of 36 islands in the Arabian sea, located 200 to 440 km off of the mainland's southwestern coast.
 
• In Malayalam, Lakshadweep means "One lakh islands".
 
• Malayalam is the official as well as the widely spoken native language in the territory.
 
• Kavaratti is the capital of the Union Territory Lakshadweep in India. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Sikkim** is the smallest state in India as per population.
 
• **Rajasthan** is the largest state in India by area.
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** is the largest state in India in terms of population.

questions.question: The earliest Buddhist texts were written in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pali.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• The earliest Buddhist texts were written in **Pali.**
 
• The Early Buddhist texts were divided into two categories- Pali and Anupali texts.
 
• Pali texts :
 
 
• Tripitaka, Deep Vansha, Maha Vansha, and Milind Pannaho are important texts.
 
• Tripitaka is the earliest and most important text in pali.
 
 
 
• Anupali texts (Sanskrit and other texts) :
 
 
• Divyavadan, Aryamanjushrimulkalpa, and Lalit Vistar are the important texts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Tripitaka **(Pali Canon), Mahayana Sutras and the Tibetan Book of the Dead are three significant no canonical Buddhist writings.
 
• The Pali Canon, which signifies “the expression of Buddha,” incorporates a portion of the Buddha’s talk, however, it additionally consolidates the lessons of his students.

• The** Cave of Bagh,** which is a marvellous vestige of Indian rock-cut architecture, is situated in **Madhya Pradesh.**

 
• Located on the bank of the Bagh river in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: The Urban learning Internship Program (TULIP), launched in June 2020, is a joint initiative of:

options.text: The Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) and Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and Ministry of Commerce and Industry
The Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA).**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

• This venture is jointly launched by the Ministry of Human Resource Development, the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, and the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE).

• Please note that the goal of MHRD and AICTE is to create 1 crore successful internships by the year 2025.
 
• TULIP is a program for providing fresh graduates with experiential learning opportunities in the urban sector.

questions.question: In honour of which saint did Akbar build Fatehpur Sikri?

• **Akbar build Fatehpur Sikri **in honour of **Sheikh Salim Chisti.**
 
• It enshrines the burial place of the Sufi saint, Salim Chisti (1478 – 1572), a descendant of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti of Ajmer, and who lived in a cavern on the ridge at Sikri.
 
• The mausoleum was constructed by Akbar as a mark of his respect for the Sufi saint.
 
• Fatehpur Sikri is a town in the Agra District of Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• The city itself was founded as the capital of the Mughal Empire in 1571 by Emperor Akbar, serving this role from 1571 to 1585, when Akbar abandoned it due to a campaign in Punjab and was later completely abandoned in 1610.

questions.question: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands comprise about ______ islands.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**572.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Andaman and Nicobar **Islands is a group of 572 islands/islets located at the juncture of the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.
 
• **Murga Island, Aves Island and Baratang Island **are some of the important islands of the Andaman Group of Islands. 
 
• Geopolitically, the ANI connects South Asia with South-East Asia.
 
• While the northernmost point of the archipelago is only 22 nautical miles from Myanmar, the southernmost point, Indira Point, is a mere 90 nautical miles from Indonesia.
 
• The islands dominate the Bay of Bengal, the Six Degree and the Ten Degree Channels that more than sixty thousand commercial vessels traverse each year.
 
• The “six-degree channel” lies between **Great Nicobar and Sumatra.**
 
• **Duncan's passage** separates **Little Andaman from South Andaman. **

questions.question: Who was the first woman to be elected as the President of Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annie Besant.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Annie Besant was the first woman to be elected as the President of the Indian National Congress.**
 
• She was elected President of the Indian National Congress at the Calcutta session in 1917.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• She was a social reformer, theosophist, and Indian independence leader.
 
• Annie Besant was born in Britain and arrived in India in 1893.
 
• Annie Besant was the second President of The Theosophical Society from 1907 to 1933.
 
• She started the Young Men’s Indian Association in 1914.
 
• Annie Besant launched the Home Rule League in September 1916 at Madras.
 
• She also started two journals: 
 
 
• The Commonweal, a weekly dealing with issues of national reform and New India, a daily newspaper which for fifteen years was a powerful instrument promoting Home Rule and revolutionizing Indian journalism.
 
 
 
• **Sucheta Kripalani** was not only the first woman Chief Minister (CM) of Uttar Pradesh (UP) but also the first woman CM of India.
 
• Indian Prime Minister** Indira Gandhi** was the first and only female Prime Minister of India.
 
 
• She was the second longest-serving Indian prime minister after her father Jawahar Lal Nehru.
 
• She was also the President of INC in 1959.

questions.question: What is the minimum age prescribed by the Constitution of India for appointment as Governor of a state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**35 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** minimum age** prescribed by the Constitution of India for appointment as Governor of a state is** 35 years.**
 
• Governor is the constitutional head of each state appointed by the president for a term of 5 years. 
 
• To become a governor of a state one should not be a member of either house of the parliament or the house of the state legislature and he should not hold any other office of profit. 
 
• Articles 153 to 167 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the state executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 25 years - Minimum age for membership in the Legislative Assembly& also Minimum age to become a member of Lok Sabha.
 
• 30 years- Minimum age for membership in the Legislative Council & also Minimum age to become a member of Rajya Sabha.
 
• 35 years- Minimum age to become a President.
 
• 18 years- Voting age of citizens of India. Before it was 21 years, but according to the 61st amendment act, it reduces to 18 years.

questions.question: India secured the _______ rank in the 12th edition of the biennial Environment Performance Index (EPI 2020) which measured the environmental performance of 180 countries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**168th.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **India secured the 168th rank in the 12th edition** of the biennial** Environment Performance Index (EPI 2020)** which measured the environmental performance of **180 countries.**
 
• The index considered 32 indicators of environmental performance and included 10-year trends in environmental performance at the national and global levels.
 
• Denmark topped the index with a score of 82.5.
 
• India scored 27.6 out of 100 in the 2020 EPI index and its performance was worse than all South Asian countries, except Afghanistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Environmental Performance Index:

 
 
• ​EPI is a biennial index prepared by Yale University and Columbia University in collaboration with the World Economic Forum.
 
• It offers a scorecard that highlights leaders and laggards in environmental performance and provides practical guidance for countries that aspire to move toward a sustainable future.
 
• This index was first published in 2002.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **As of May 2022:**

 
 
• **India **has been ranked at the **bottom **in a **list of 180 countries **that were judged for their environmental performances in the 2022 Environmental Performance Index (EPI).
 
• The list is headed by Denmark, which is seen as the world’s most sustainable country.

questions.question: Which acid does vinegar contain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acetic acid.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Vinegar is a sour liquid** that is made by the fermentation of numerous dilute alcoholic liquids into a liquid **containing acetic acid.**
 
• Vinegar can be made from any liquid that is capable of being converted into alcohol in a two-step process. 
 
• Vinegar usually contains 5–8 per cent of ac**etic acid **by volume.
 
• Acetic acid is typically formed by the fermentation of ethanol or sugars by acetic acid bacteria.
 
• Vinegar is primarily used in the culinary arts: as a flavorful, acidic.
 
• The conversion of ethanol(CH3CH2OH) and oxygen(O2) to acetic acid(CH3COOH) are followed by the following reaction:
 
 
• CH3CH2OH + O2 → CH3COOH + H2O

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India provides that Hindi in Devanagari script shall be the official language of the Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 343 (1)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 343(1) in The Constitution Of India 1949

 
 
• ​The official language of the Union shall be Hindi in the Devanagari script.
 
• The form of numerals to be used for the official purposes of the Union shall be the international form of Indian numerals.
 
 
 
• **Article 343(2), **1949 in the Indian constitution of India states that the English language shall continue to be used as the official language.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Eighth Schedule** to the Constitution consists of the following 22 languages:-

 
 
• (1) Assamese, (2) Bengali, (3) Gujarati, (4) Hindi, (5) Kannada, (6) Kashmiri, (7) Konkani, (8) Malayalam, (9) Manipuri, (10) Marathi, (11) Nepali, (12) Oriya, (13) Punjabi, (14) Sanskrit, (15) Sindhi, (16) Tamil, (17) Telugu, (18) Urdu (19) Bodo, (20) Santhali, (21) Maithili (22) Dogri. 
 
 
 
• Of these languages, 14 were initially included in the Constitution. The Sindhi language was added in 1967.
 
• Thereafter three more languages viz., Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were included in 1992. Subsequently, Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added in 2004.

questions.question: Which of the following is called the Powerhouse of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria.**__

• **Mitochondria **are the sites of aerobic respiration.
 
• They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called ‘power houses’ of the cell.
 
• The mitochondria are the site for aerobic respiration releasing energy in the form of ATP.
 
• Mitochondria are membrane-bound organelles present in all eukaryotic cells' cytoplasm.</span
